arrivals_per_day.citation: CMS Care Compare 'Timely and Effective Care - Hospital' (Provider Data Catalog yv7e-xc69, release 2026-08-13), Facility ID (CCN) 310038 ROBERT WOOD JOHNSON UNIVERSITY HOSPITAL, ONE ROBERT WOOD JOHNSON PLACE, NEW BRUNSWICK NJ; OP_22 denominator 81126 ED visits in 01/01/2024-12/31/2024 / 366 days
arrivals_per_day.note: All ED visits billed under the CMS number, pediatric ED included. Upper end of range = the hospital's own 'more than 95,000 emergency and trauma patients a year' / 365 (Wave 0 value 260). Hourly, weekday and seasonal variation come from the arrival_*_profile attributes.

arrival_hour_profile.citation: CDC/NCHS NHAMCS Emergency Department public-use microdata, 2019+2021+2022 pooled (51,713 sampled visits; 2020 excluded), weighted by PATWT; variable ARRTIME (arrival time, hour part), all hospitals, 50393 visits with a recorded time; weighted visits per hour divided by the 24-hour mean
arrival_hour_profile.note: National shape, not this hospital's. 2.7% of weighted visits have no arrival time and are excluded.

arrival_dow_profile.citation: CDC/NCHS NHAMCS Emergency Department public-use microdata, 2019+2021+2022 pooled (51,713 sampled visits; 2020 excluded), weighted by PATWT; variable VDAYR (1=Sunday..7=Saturday) re-indexed Monday first, all hospitals; weighted visits per weekday divided by the 7-day mean
arrival_dow_profile.note: National shape. Each sampled hospital reports a 4-week period, so weekdays are evenly represented.

arrival_month_profile.citation: Placeholder set in Wave 0 so the simulator can run; winter respiratory season
arrival_month_profile.note: STILL ASSUMED after checking two sources. (1) NHAMCS cannot support a month profile: each hospital reports one 4-week period, and the pooled 8-year estimate [1.1074, 0.9721, 0.9869, 1.0984, 0.9768, 0.8592, 0.9082, 1.2781, 1.0944, 0.8926, 1.0292, 0.7967] has a between-year SD of 0.13-0.41 per month (data/processed/nhamcs_ed_arrival_profiles.json) - noise, not seasonality. (2) CDC ILINet (HHS Region 2) gives the seasonal SHAPE of influenza-like illness only: monthly mean wILI percent [5.189, 5.246, 3.69, 2.659, 2.103, 1.686, 1.417, 1.395, 1.848, 2.444, 3.402, 5.266] (data/processed/fluview_ili_summary.json), i.e. a winter excess of roughly 2-4 percent of visits over summer, consistent in direction with the assumed winter multipliers of 1.02-1.06 but not a measurement of total ED volume.

acuity_mix.citation: CDC/NCHS NHAMCS Emergency Department public-use microdata, 2019+2021+2022 pooled (51,713 sampled visits; 2020 excluded), weighted by PATWT; variable IMMEDR (triage level 1 immediate .. 5 nonurgent), metropolitan hospitals with an emergency medicine residency (MSA==1 & EMEDRES==1; 19,992 sampled visits); shares among visits with a recorded level 1-5 (unweighted n by level [270, 2326, 6762, 3479, 516])
acuity_mix.note: IMMEDR is not imputed: only 69% of weighted visits in this subset carry a level 1-5 (the rest are unknown, blank, 'no triage', or in an ED without nursing triage) and are EXCLUDED, i.e. assumed to have the same mix. NHAMCS rescales hospitals' 3- and 4-level scales to 5 levels, so level 1 is noisier than a true ESI 1. All-hospital mix for comparison: [0.02286, 0.14692, 0.5071, 0.28895, 0.03416].

condition_mix.citation: CDC/NCHS NHAMCS Emergency Department public-use microdata, 2019+2021+2022 pooled (51,713 sampled visits; 2020 excluded), weighted by PATWT; variable RFV13D (first-listed reason for visit, NCHS Reason for Visit Classification) mapped by us to nine groups, metropolitan hospitals with an emergency medicine residency (MSA==1 & EMEDRES==1; 19,992 sampled visits)
condition_mix.note: The code-range -> condition_group mapping is ours (listed under condition_mapping in the extract and in research/operations-data-sources.md); groups are by presenting complaint, not final diagnosis. Mix by acuity: data/processed/nhamcs_ed_condition_by_acuity.csv.

arrival_mode_mix.citation: CDC/NCHS NHAMCS Emergency Department public-use microdata, 2019+2021+2022 pooled (51,713 sampled visits; 2020 excluded), weighted by PATWT; variables ARREMS (arrival by ambulance) and AMBTRANSFER (ambulance arrival transferred from another hospital or urgent care), metropolitan hospitals with an emergency medicine residency (MSA==1 & EMEDRES==1; 19,992 sampled visits)
arrival_mode_mix.note: transfer = ambulance arrivals transferred from another facility; transfers arriving by other means are not identifiable and sit in walk_in. 3.2% unknown arrival mode excluded.

ambulance_share_by_acuity.citation: CDC/NCHS NHAMCS Emergency Department public-use microdata, 2019+2021+2022 pooled (51,713 sampled visits; 2020 excluded), weighted by PATWT; share with ARREMS==1 among visits with known arrival mode, by IMMEDR level, metropolitan hospitals with an emergency medicine residency (MSA==1 & EMEDRES==1; 19,992 sampled visits)
ambulance_share_by_acuity.note: Includes inter-facility transfers by ambulance. Level 5 is not lower than level 4 in the data (small cell: 516 visits). All-hospital values: [0.368, 0.356, 0.181, 0.06, 0.081].

age_band_mix.citation: CDC/NCHS NHAMCS Emergency Department public-use microdata, 2019+2021+2022 pooled (51,713 sampled visits; 2020 excluded), weighted by PATWT; variable AGE, metropolitan hospitals with an emergency medicine residency (MSA==1 & EMEDRES==1; 19,992 sampled visits)
age_band_mix.note: All ages, including children (this subset contains children's hospitals; the all-hospital share under 18 is 0.214). RWJUH runs a separate pediatric ED under the same CMS number; if the simulated stream is adults only, renormalise the three adult bands.

payer_mix.citation: CDC/NCHS NHAMCS Emergency Department public-use microdata, 2019+2021+2022 pooled (51,713 sampled visits; 2020 excluded), weighted by PATWT; variable PAYTYPER (recoded primary expected source of payment), metropolitan hospitals with an emergency medicine residency (MSA==1 & EMEDRES==1; 19,992 sampled visits)
payer_mix.note: Mapping: private->commercial; Medicaid/CHIP->medicaid; self-pay + no charge/charity->self_pay; workers' compensation + other->other. 11.3% unknown/blank payer excluded. National teaching-hospital mix, not New Jersey's or this hospital's.

payer_revenue_multiplier.citation: Placeholder set in Wave 0 so the simulator can run; placeholder payment-to-Medicare ratios

inpatient_los_days.citation: CDC/NCHS NHAMCS Emergency Department public-use microdata, 2019+2021+2022 pooled (51,713 sampled visits; 2020 excluded), weighted by PATWT; variable LOS (length of hospital stay in days for visits admitted to this hospital, ADMITHOS==1), all hospitals, n=5850 admissions with a known stay; mean capped at 60 days
inpatient_los_days.note: Median 4 days, 90th percentile 10. range is the interquartile range. Stays of patients admitted through the ED only.

inpatient_revenue.citation: CMS IPPS FY 2027 final rule + correction notice: Tables 1A/1D standardized amounts (labor 4519.68, nonlabor 2328.32, capital 539.95) and Impact File row for CCN 310038 (wage index 1.2727, teaching factor 0.18135, DSH factor 0.04234, capital GAF 1.1795501088188711, transfer-adjusted case-mix index 2.461, uncompensated-care amount per claim 1847.02); operating = (labor*wage_index + nonlabor) * (1 + TCHOP + DSHOPP); capital = capital_rate * GAF * (1 + TCHCP + DSHCPP); payment(weight) = (operating + capital) * weight + UCP per claim. Outliers, VBP/readmission/HAC adjustments, new-technology add-ons and transfers ignored.
inpatient_revenue.note: Medicare fee-for-service basis (other payers through payer_revenue_multiplier). BASE-RATE ASSUMPTION: the stay is paid at this hospital's average Medicare case-mix index (2.461, all Medicare discharges including transplant and cardiac surgery); medical admissions through the ED are on average lighter, so this is an upper estimate - lower end of range = a DRG weight of 1.0 (12492 usd). Payment per unit of DRG weight = 10645 usd. Cross-check: the hospital's FY2024 cost report gives net patient revenue 1,665,310,131 usd x inpatient share of charges 0.689 / 36,561 discharges = about 31,400 usd per discharge, all payers. MS-DRG weights and mean LOS: data/processed/ipps_fy2027_table5_msdrg.csv.

deterioration_hazard_per_hour_waiting.citation: Rizer NW, Klein E, Copenhaver MS, Zhao X, Kelen GD, Hinson JS (2026) Early Clinical Deterioration Among Emergency Department Boarders: A Retrospective Analysis, Ann Emerg Med 87(6):681-693 (abstract): of 173,168 floor-level medical admissions boarding 4-48 h at five hospitals, 6,299 (3.6%) escalated to intermediate or intensive care within 48 h of the admission order, 2,823 (45%) of them while still in the ED; median boarding 12.5 h (IQR 8.2-20.7) with deterioration vs 10.2 h without; +0.8% relative risk overall and +2.4% for in-ED deterioration per extra boarding hour; 28-day mortality 13.0% after deterioration vs 3.9%.
deterioration_hazard_per_hour_waiting.note: DERIVED by the research agent for ESI 2 and 3 only: 3.6% / 12.5 h = 0.0029 per hour (ESI 2 value 0.003); in-ED events only, 1.6% / 12.5 h = 0.0013 (low end); ESI 3 set to a third of ESI 2 because most ESI 3 patients are discharged. The source measures admitted patients boarding after treatment, not untreated patients in the waiting room; no waiting-room deterioration rate was found. ESI 1, 4 and 5 values are unchanged Wave 0 placeholders and remain ASSUMED. US academic system, 2018-2024.
deterioration_hazard_per_hour_waiting.mixed_provenance: PER-ELEMENT PROVENANCE (audit 2026-10-10): only the ESI 2 value is computed from the cited source; ESI 3 is an assumed fraction of it; ESI 1, 4 and 5 are ASSUMED placeholders.

death_hazard_per_hour_untreated.citation: Derived from (a) Singer AJ et al. (2011) Acad Emerg Med, 41,256 admissions: in-hospital mortality 2.5% boarded <2 h vs 4.5% boarded >=12 h (about 0.0017 per hour); (b) Jones S et al. (2022) Emerg Med J, 5.25 million admitted patients, England: 30-day mortality rises linearly from 5 to 12 h after arrival, one extra death per 82 patients delayed beyond 6-8 h; (c) Guttmann A et al. (2011) BMJ, 13.9 million discharged patients, Ontario: 8,502 deaths among 6.64 million high-acuity and 1,998 among 7.29 million low-acuity discharged patients within 7 days, and one hour less mean stay estimated to avoid 6.5% and 12.7% of them (about 8e-5 and 4e-5 per patient-hour). ESI 2 = admitted-patient figure; ESI 3 = 30% admitted-type + 70% discharged high-acuity; ESI 4-5 = discharged low-acuity.
death_hazard_per_hour_untreated.note: DERIVED by the research agent; observational, confounded, and these are attributable deaths within 7 to 30 days per hour of delay, not deaths inside the department. ESI 1 (0.01) has no usable source and remains ASSUMED: ESI 1 patients are treated immediately by definition. Other URLs: https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1553-2712.2011.01236.x (Singer), https://doi.org/10.1136/emermed-2021-211572 (Jones). In Jones the effect starts about 5 h after arrival; applying the hazard from minute zero overstates harm for short waits.
death_hazard_per_hour_untreated.mixed_provenance: PER-ELEMENT PROVENANCE (audit 2026-10-10): the ESI 1 value is an ASSUMED placeholder; ESI 2-5 are derived from the cited sources.

lwbs_patience_min.citation: Batt RJ, Terwiesch C (2015) Waiting Patiently: An Empirical Study of Queue Abandonment in an Emergency Department, Management Science 61(1):39-59 (working-paper PDF read). Table 1: mean wait 1.0/1.9/1.3/1.3 h and LWBS 1.7%/9.5%/4.7%/7.4% for ESI 2/3/4/5 (N = 27,538/65,773/39,878/10,509); 'ESI 1 patients ... do not abandon'. Values are the exponential mean patience that reproduces each LWBS share at that mean wait: theta = -wait / ln(1 - LWBS), rounded.
lwbs_patience_min.note: DERIVED by the research agent from a published table, not a published estimate. One US urban academic ED, about 180,000 visits. ESI 1 is set effectively infinite (they did not leave). The same paper's regression gives about +0.5 percentage points LWBS per extra 15 min of wait for ESI 3 (hazard about 0.02/h, mean 3,000 min), hence the wide range. Patience also falls with visible queue length (one more person in the waiting room = +0.5 points). The Wave 0 placeholder (240 min for ESI 3) would give about 38% LWBS at a 1.9 h wait, four times the observed 9.5%.

boarding_los_penalty.unit: fraction of inpatient LOS per boarding hour
boarding_los_penalty.citation: Singer AJ, Thode HC, Viccellio P, Pines JM (2011) The association between length of emergency department boarding and mortality, Acad Emerg Med 18(12): mean hospital stay 5.6 days when boarded <2 h vs 8.7 days when boarded >24 h (41,256 admissions, one US academic ED, unadjusted) = at most about +2.3% of stay per boarding hour. Roussel M et al. (2023) JAMA Intern Med: patients aged 75+ who spent the night in the ED had length-of-stay rate ratio 1.20 (1.11-1.31). Sun BC et al. (2013) Ann Emerg Med: admission on a high-crowding day = +0.8% length of stay (995,379 admissions, adjusted).
boarding_los_penalty.note: Loose range; value set inside it. The unadjusted single-site figure (0.023) is the ceiling because sicker patients board longer; the adjusted multi-hospital figure is far smaller. US and France.

treatment_min.citation: CDC/NCHS NHAMCS Emergency Department public-use microdata, 2019+2021+2022 pooled (51,713 sampled visits; 2020 excluded), weighted by PATWT; weighted least-squares of (LOV - WAITTIME - BOARDED) minutes on triage-level dummies + X-ray, CT, MRI, ultrasound, lab and admission indicators, metropolitan hospitals with an emergency medicine residency (MSA==1 & EMEDRES==1; 19,992 sampled visits), n=10580 visits (5392 at level 3); value = the level-3 coefficient = mean minutes from first provider contact to leaving the ED for a visit with no imaging and no lab
treatment_min.note: Model-derived, R2=0.167; outcome winsorized at the 99th percentile; cv is the raw coefficient of variation of the outcome at this level. Test-attributable minutes in the same model: X-ray 21.1, CT 69.0, MRI 177.4, ultrasound 38.9, lab 83.1, admitted -27.2. Observed mean after provider contact at this level incl. tests: 233.2 (median 182.0). The value includes provider re-evaluation and discharge processing, so if the simulator adds those separately it should be recalibrated against the length-of-visit targets in catalog/validation_targets.yaml.

p_imaging.citation: CDC/NCHS NHAMCS Emergency Department public-use microdata, 2019+2021+2022 pooled (51,713 sampled visits; 2020 excluded), weighted by PATWT; ANYIMAGE (any imaging ordered or provided); IMMEDR==3, metropolitan hospitals with an emergency medicine residency (MSA==1 & EMEDRES==1; 19,992 sampled visits), n=6762
p_imaging.note: National estimate for triage level 3; all_hospitals value 0.632. Visits that left without being seen and DOA excluded.

p_ct_given_imaging.citation: CDC/NCHS NHAMCS Emergency Department public-use microdata, 2019+2021+2022 pooled (51,713 sampled visits; 2020 excluded), weighted by PATWT; CATSCAN==1 among visits with ANYIMAGE==1; IMMEDR==3, metropolitan hospitals with an emergency medicine residency (MSA==1 & EMEDRES==1; 19,992 sampled visits), n=3721
p_ct_given_imaging.note: National estimate for triage level 3; all_hospitals value 0.470. Visits that left without being seen and DOA excluded.

p_lab.citation: CDC/NCHS NHAMCS Emergency Department public-use microdata, 2019+2021+2022 pooled (51,713 sampled visits; 2020 excluded), weighted by PATWT; any of 22 blood/urine/culture/toxicology items (CBC, BMP, CMP, cardiac enzymes, urinalysis, cultures ...); rapid flu/COVID/pregnancy/HIV tests not counted; IMMEDR==3, metropolitan hospitals with an emergency medicine residency (MSA==1 & EMEDRES==1; 19,992 sampled visits), n=6762
p_lab.note: National estimate for triage level 3; all_hospitals value 0.695. Visits that left without being seen and DOA excluded.

p_admit.citation: CDC/NCHS NHAMCS Emergency Department public-use microdata, 2019+2021+2022 pooled (51,713 sampled visits; 2020 excluded), weighted by PATWT; ADMITHOS==1 or OBSHOS==1 (admitted to this hospital, directly or via observation unit); IMMEDR==3, metropolitan hospitals with an emergency medicine residency (MSA==1 & EMEDRES==1; 19,992 sampled visits), n=6762

revenue_ed_visit.citation: CMS OPPS Addendum B, July 2026 update (national unadjusted payment rate by HCPCS code), wage-adjusted for CCN 310038 as rate x (0.6 x wage index 1.2727 + 0.4) = x1.1636; HCPCS 99284 (APC 5024), national rate 426.3
revenue_ed_visit.note: MAPPING ASSUMPTION: triage level 3 is billed as visit code 99284 (level 1 -> critical care first hour, levels 2-5 -> ED visit levels 5-2; the lowest visit level 99281 is not used). In practice the billed level follows documented resources, not the triage level. Hospital facility payment on the Medicare basis only: no physician professional fee; many ancillaries are packaged into it.
